data.description:
TB-29 fixed --exclude-subagents on the RAW path (is_subagent path detection). The
AGENTSVIEW path was never covered, and there the flag does nothing at all.

MEASURED (live archive, --agent claude --all --limit 40, 2026-07-13):

  raw path (TB-29 fix works):
    [none]                620 calls, fingerprint 332fff82da4be971
    [--exclude-subagents] 521 calls, fingerprint 5c3854a59d2c2641   <- moves, correct

  agentsview path (no-op):
    [none]                3251 calls, fingerprint 6d146170ac125aff
    [--exclude-subagents] 3251 calls, fingerprint 6d146170ac125aff  <- IDENTICAL

Identical call count AND identical corpus fingerprint with the flag on and off:
nothing was excluded. But the Summary still flips its provenance line to
'Subagents included: no' -- an unearned claim. The report asserts an exclusion
that demonstrably did not occur.

ROOT CAUSE: shares TB-30's root cause. Without --include-children, agentsview never
LISTS subagent/child sessions, so no ref ever carries is_subagent=True and the
filter has nothing to remove. TB-29 hardened the predicate; this path never
receives the rows to apply it to.

NOTE ON ORDERING: fixing TB-30 (passing --include-children) is necessary but likely
not sufficient -- once child sessions are listed, is_subagent must actually be
derived for agentsview-sourced refs, which have path=None and so cannot use the
raw path's '<project>/<session-uuid>/subagents/' path-segment detection. The
agentsview row shape must supply the signal (e.g. a parent/child field on the
session-list JSON). Fix TB-30 first, then re-run this A/B: if the fingerprint still
does not move, the is_subagent derivation is the remaining gap.

FIX: after TB-30, derive is_subagent for agentsview refs from the session-list
payload, and assert in tests that --exclude-subagents moves the fingerprint on BOTH
index sources (the TB-29 test asserted on the FILTERED refs -- mirror that here).
The 'Subagents included:' provenance line should reflect what was actually filtered,
not merely which flag was passed.

Found by: operator smoke checkpoint CP3 (EVALUATION.md), 2026-07-13.
data.title: --exclude-subagents is a silent no-op on the agentsview index path, and the Summary claims an exclusion that never happened

data.body:
FIXED in PR #53, shipped together with TB-30 (they are one bug wearing two hats).

THE FIX AS FILED IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE. The ticket proposed deriving is_subagent 'from the
session-list payload (e.g. a parent/child field on the session-list JSON)'. There is no such
field. I validated every candidate predicate against ground truth (the exact set difference
between --include-children on and off, 923 real child sessions):

  source_session_id != id     TP 915/923, FP 1631  <- ALSO fires on resumed/compacted
                                                      sessions. Would have silently
                                                      misclassified 1631 legitimate top-level
                                                      sessions as subagents. A cure worse
                                                      than the disease.
  id matches ^(scheme:)?agent-  TP 915/923, FP 0    <- precise, but misses 7 codex subagents
                                                      that carry neither an agent- token nor
                                                      a parent pointer. They are unambiguously
                                                      real: their first messages are dispatched
                                                      task prompts ('Your read-only task:',
                                                      'Final review ... Do not edit files').

So the implementation does not guess. It lists TWICE -- once with --include-children withheld
-- and takes the difference. That IS agentsview's own definition of 'child'. Zero FP, zero FN,
catches the codex 7, and survives a change to the id scheme. Cost: one extra metadata-only
pass, ~5s for the whole 11.9k archive, proportionally less for any scoped run since the probe
inherits the same --agent/--project/--since filters.

WHY TRUTHFUL STAMPING AT DISCOVERY IS MANDATORY (not just nice): freeze persists is_subagent,
and freeze.py's stale-'false' self-heal can only fall back to the PATH -- which agentsview refs
do not have (path=None). Leave the stamp false and every frozen agentsview corpus keeps
--exclude-subagents lying on replay forever.

VERIFIED, the A/B that used to be a no-op (--agent claude --all --limit 200):
  subagents included    200 discovered, 200 scanned, fp 5b60fb05f73527d5
  --exclude-subagents   200 discovered, 183 scanned, fp 1256cff318b8381b   <- MOVES
  (200 - 17 = 183). Freeze/replay: manifest stamps 18, replay scans 182. Both correct.

CAUTION ON THIS TICKET'S ORIGINAL EVIDENCE: the filed A/B used --limit 40. The 40 most-recent
claude sessions contain ZERO subagents -- the first child sits at recency position 93 -- so
that experiment could not have moved the fingerprint whether or not the filter worked. The
diagnosis was correct; the experiment was not decisive. The regression test now pins a window
that actually contains children.

Provenance line is now earned rather than asserted: it reports the count actually stamped at
discovery ('no (17 of 200 discovered excluded)'), so a 'no' beside '0 of N' says the index
found no subagents -- not that the filter did its job.

provenance.reason: Fix designed: three --include-* flags + parent-probe set difference for is_subagent
PR #53 open; 511 tests pass, ruff + mypy --strict clean; verified end-to-end on the live archive
